intro.title: Will you two agree?
intro.nima: I'm Nima, your guide. Every choice in your plan has two doors: what happens if nothing changes, and what happens with your plan. Each of you reads it your own way, then you meet.

intro.second: {partner} has already ranked theirs. Will you agree?

card_why.text: You pay $300 a month on the card. $270 of it is interest. At this pace it is paid off in September 2039.

retire.text: Your retirement is on track. In the plan, your savings never run out.
retire.label: you retire at 62 and 60
retire.detail: Income covers 93% of your yearly need in retirement. The plan ends with $2,371,900 in savings, in today's dollars. You save 22.8% of what you earn.

timothy.text: The Chase card is in your name. The cash that could pay it is in Melanie's account. This one needs both of you.

timothy.text: $12,740 of your Roth is in a leveraged fund: it moves more than the market, up and down. Your plan asks you and Melanie to agree on how much risk you want.
timothy.label: in a leveraged fund
timothy.detail: That is about half of your $25,000 Roth. Over three years the account returned 41.1% with 30% volatility, and your plan says that may not repeat. Not urgent, but worth watching.

ask.q: Why pay the card if we have cash?
ask.a: Of every $300 you pay on the card, $270 is interest. Meanwhile $60,222 of your cash sits above your reserve and near-term goals, earning about 0.1%.

ask.q: How much life cover do we have?
ask.a: Your life cover is $140,000 and $110,000. Your plan recommends $750,000 to $1,500,000 for Timothy and $600,000 to $1,200,000 for Melanie. The first step it scores is $235,000 more.

ask.q: What is an umbrella policy for?
ask.a: It pays if someone claims a large amount from you, for example after an accident. Nothing covers that today, and your net worth is $695,500. Your plan suggests a $1,000,000 policy.

ask.q: How much is missing for college?
ask.a: Nothing is saved yet. The gap for both children is $113,508.60, about $4,609 a year.

ask.q: Does life cover alone raise our score?
ask.a: No. On its own the score stays at 60, because the 18% card holds it there. Together with the card paydown it reaches 73.
Your plan scores 60 today. Paying down the card reaches 62, card plus life cover 73, and adding the umbrella 78.

ask.q: How much cash do we have?
ask.a: You hold $150,800 in cash. About $60,000 of it sits above your reserve and near-term goals.

nima_hello: Ask me anything, at any moment. If your plan has the answer, I show you where it comes from. If it doesn't, I tell you and pass it to your advisor.
